flows.title: Undergraduate research training workflow
flows.summary: The main route covers all 7 stages. Decision nodes state when to continue; side branches show where to return if conditions are not met.
flows.note: This is a guide to the work involved. Learning, research and writing may overlap. Formal approval, recognition of outputs and degree conferral follow the rules applicable to you and your institution's decisions.

nodes.label: Orientation and mutual fit
nodes.detail: Agree on goals, time, resources and communication.

nodes.label: Do the task and available time fit?
nodes.detail: Both parties confirm the scope and review date.

nodes.label: Revise and review
nodes.detail: Reduce the task, strengthen foundations or adjust the schedule. Pause or leave the training if it is not a suitable fit.

nodes.label: Tools, literature and research practice
nodes.detail: Set up the environment and establish reading and evidence-recording habits.

nodes.label: Reading, replication and small tasks
nodes.detail: Use small reading and replication tasks to test whether a question merits research.

nodes.label: Does the evidence justify continuing?
nodes.detail: Explain the replication results, value and resource requirements.

nodes.label: Revise and review
nodes.detail: Check data and environment issues first. If the question lacks value, change it or stop, preserving negative findings.

nodes.label: Project plan and task breakdown
nodes.detail: Define milestones, responsibilities and verifiable deliverables.

nodes.label: Execution, weekly reports and reviews
nodes.detail: Keep versions and logs; use feedback to plan the next tasks.

nodes.label: Result verification and communication
nodes.detail: Check claims, contributions, citations and permission to publish.

nodes.label: Can the results be checked?
nodes.detail: Key claims match actual records, and usage permissions are clear.

nodes.label: Revise and review
nodes.detail: Add experiments or narrow the claims. Withhold material without clear permission, and review again before closing the project.

nodes.label: Closure, archiving and next steps
nodes.detail: Complete acceptance, reflection and follow-on arrangements.

edges.label: Return to reading and small tests

flows.title: Undergraduate capstone / thesis workflow
flows.summary: The main route covers all 8 stages. Decision nodes state when to continue; side branches show where to return if conditions are not met.
flows.note: This is a guide to the work involved. Learning, research and writing may overlap. Formal approval, recognition of outputs and degree conferral follow the rules applicable to you and your institution's decisions.

nodes.label: Requirements, topic and task brief
nodes.detail: Check formal requirements; agree on scope and individual responsibilities.

nodes.label: Literature review and proposal
nodes.detail: Prepare the review, research question, approach and proposal materials.

nodes.label: Does the formal proposal meet requirements?
nodes.detail: Follow the department's official decision and required revisions.

nodes.label: Revise and review
nodes.detail: Revise the topic, approach or validation plan in response to feedback, and seek a new review as instructed.

nodes.label: Requirements analysis and detailed design
nodes.detail: Connect core requirements to design decisions and acceptance methods.

nodes.label: Implementation and mid-program review
nodes.detail: Complete core functions and submit an accurate progress record.

nodes.label: Are mid-program conditions met?
nodes.detail: Check core implementation, the official review outcome and remaining tasks.

nodes.label: Revise and review
nodes.detail: Prioritize missing core functionality, record corrections and review again. A plan is not completed work.

nodes.label: Testing, experiments and analysis
nodes.detail: Address the main goals, retaining failure and boundary-case evidence.

nodes.label: Thesis writing and compliance checks
nodes.detail: Complete the argument, references, formatting and required institutional checks.

nodes.label: Defense preparation and participation
nodes.detail: Check eligibility and materials, prepare a verifiable demonstration and attend the formal defense.

nodes.label: Does the official defense decision allow finalization?
nodes.detail: Fulfil every condition, including revisions required for a conditional pass.

nodes.label: Revise and review
nodes.detail: Revise, seek further review or reapply under institutional rules. Report demonstration failures accurately.

nodes.label: Final revisions, archiving and handover
nodes.detail: Address defense feedback, submit institutional materials and hand over research records.

edges.label: Return to proposal revision and review
Return to thesis revisions and application

flows.title: Competitions and innovation workflow
flows.summary: The main route covers all 6 stages. Decision nodes state when to continue; side branches show where to return if conditions are not met.
flows.note: Plan registration independently around the official window. Registration and prototyping may overlap or occur in a different order under the rules; do not miss a deadline while awaiting an internal milestone. Each restricted activity still requires its formal prerequisites. This diagram guides the work; official decisions determine eligibility and results.

nodes.label: Competition, eligibility and rules
nodes.detail: Check the track, eligibility, current rules and official deadlines.

nodes.label: Are eligibility and rules confirmed?
nodes.detail: Use the current official notice, not assumptions from previous editions.

nodes.label: Revise and review
nodes.detail: Change track or stop if ineligible. Ask the organizer about unclear rules before committing resources.

nodes.label: Team, topic and ownership agreement
nodes.detail: Agree on roles, project scope and ownership of materials and outputs.

nodes.label: Prototype, budget and registration
nodes.detail: Track registration separately; develop the prototype and budget against the event schedule.

nodes.label: Current work prerequisites and registration plan clear?
nodes.detail: Meet eligibility and budget conditions for the current activity; continue tracking registration status.

nodes.label: Revise and review
nodes.detail: Revise the approach, correct registration or reduce the budget. Stop and record the reason if unresolved.

nodes.label: Implementation, replication and internal acceptance
nodes.detail: Check the project against scoring criteria, versions and licenses.

nodes.label: Does the project meet submission conditions?
nodes.detail: Match scoring criteria, permissions, functionality and material versions item by item.

nodes.label: Revise and review
nodes.detail: Fix defects or remove unreliable features. Replace noncompliant components, then repeat acceptance checks.

nodes.label: Submission, competition and confirmed results
nodes.detail: Keep submission receipts. Record awards only from official results.

nodes.label: Reflection, expense settlement and archiving
nodes.detail: Complete the review, settle expenses and equipment, and archive authorized materials.

edges.label: Return to scope and team agreements

flows.title: Master's research and degree workflow
flows.summary: The main route covers all 13 stages. Decision nodes state when to continue; side branches show where to return if conditions are not met.
flows.note: This is a guide to the work involved. Learning, research and writing may overlap. Formal approval, recognition of outputs and degree conferral follow the rules applicable to you and your institution's decisions. Check separately whether a pre-defense is required and where it falls in relation to screening and thesis review.

nodes.label: Enrollment, study plan and working agreements
nodes.detail: Check training and outcome requirements at entry; agree on communication and reviews.

nodes.label: Exploration and topic selection
nodes.detail: Select a question using actual needs, preliminary tests and available resources.

nodes.label: Literature review and research positioning
nodes.detail: Search, read and compare work to explain how your study relates to it.

nodes.label: Research plan and formal proposal review
nodes.detail: Align the question, methods, evaluation and schedule; attend the formal proposal review.

nodes.label: Is the proposal approved or revision completed?
nodes.detail: Use institutional procedures for a new review or substantial changes.

nodes.label: Revise and review
nodes.detail: Address feedback, narrowing the topic or changing methods where needed. Apply for a new review if required and retain the official decision.

nodes.label: Research, professional practice and records
nodes.detail: Build verifiable evidence through actual execution, practice and weekly reports.

nodes.label: Mid-program review and annual assessment
nodes.detail: Check research progress and all compulsory components against the notice.

nodes.label: Review conditions met and core claims supported?
nodes.detail: Assess formal review and research completion separately; outline and methods drafting can proceed in parallel.

nodes.label: Revise and review
nodes.detail: Return to research for missing core evidence; address an unsuccessful formal review through its own process and record both states.

nodes.label: Thesis structure, draft and revision
nodes.detail: Build the argument from available results; preserve supervisory feedback and revisions.

nodes.label: Research outputs and degree eligibility
nodes.detail: Complete the final verification of requirements checked from entry and the supporting evidence.

nodes.label: Formatting, similarity, error and AI-use checks
nodes.detail: Distinguish similarity screening, non-academic-error checks and AI-use disclosure.

nodes.label: Are eligibility and all checks confirmed?
nodes.detail: Verify output, similarity, non-academic-error and AI requirements separately.

nodes.label: Revise and review
nodes.detail: Address the specific cause: add evidence, revise, repeat checks or change the application date. Do not invent thresholds.

nodes.label: Anonymous thesis review and responses
nodes.detail: Freeze the submitted version, arrange anonymous review and address each comment.

nodes.label: Is defense eligibility formally confirmed?
nodes.detail: Follow official decisions on reviews, further review or appeals.

nodes.label: Revise and review
nodes.detail: Respond item by item; revise, seek further review or defer as required. Do not privately influence reviewers.

nodes.label: Defense application and formal defense
nodes.detail: Meet official prerequisites, apply and attend the formal defense.

nodes.label: Does the official decision allow the next steps?
nodes.detail: Passing the defense does not mean the degree has been conferred.

nodes.label: Revise and review
nodes.detail: Revise or reapply according to the formal decision and institutional timetable.

nodes.label: Final revisions and degree procedures
nodes.detail: Obtain revision confirmation, submit the final thesis and complete degree procedures.

nodes.label: Research archive, handover and departure
nodes.detail: Complete research-material acceptance and transfer access and responsibilities separately.

nodes.label: Positioning and feasibility still supported?
nodes.detail: Check whether the question is already resolved and essential data are accessible.

nodes.label: Revise the question and search
nodes.detail: Return to topic selection with the comparison matrix; reassess literature and resources for the revised question.

edges.label: Return to topic and proposal revisions
Return to research and missing requirements
Return to writing and eligibility checks
Return to thesis revision and further review

flows.title: Doctoral research and degree pathway
flows.summary: 11 stages connect the research agenda, original contributions and formal degree milestones, with routes for revision and further evidence.
flows.note: Complete qualification only where required by your programme. Follow institutional rules for its order relative to the proposal, any pre-defense and thesis review. Annual and interim reviews recur throughout research; their position here is for navigation. Research, literature review and writing iterate, and outcome requirements are checked from entry. Passing the defense does not itself confer the degree.

nodes.label: Programme Requirements, Supervision and Development Plan
nodes.detail: Confirm applicable rules, outcome criteria, language and supervision arrangements.

nodes.label: Foundations, Research Methods and a Map of Questions
nodes.detail: Build a literature comparison, problem map and feasibility evidence.

nodes.label: Qualifying Assessment and Research Readiness, Where Applicable
nodes.detail: Confirm whether qualification applies, its order and format, then complete the required assessment.

nodes.label: Requirements due at this point confirmed and met?
nodes.detail: Use your programme sequence: record a later qualification milestone if scheduled after the proposal, or the basis if it does not apply. Uncertainty is not an exemption.

nodes.label: Revise and recheck
nodes.detail: Address foundational gaps, reassessment or plan changes and retain the formal outcome.

nodes.label: Research Direction, Linked Studies and Formal Proposal
nodes.detail: Justify the problem, original contribution, methods and contingency plans.

nodes.label: Proposal approved and required corrections completed?
nodes.detail: Confirm major changes in direction or methods through the required process.

nodes.label: Revise and recheck
nodes.detail: Revise the question, methods and resources in response to review; seek reassessment where required.

nodes.label: Independent Research, Evidence Testing and Iteration
nodes.detail: Conduct research and test counterexamples, alternative explanations and key assumptions.

nodes.label: Ongoing Annual Reflection, Interim Assessment and Replanning
nodes.detail: Revisit progress, requirements and the research agenda at scheduled reviews.

nodes.label: Current review and evidence conditions met?
nodes.detail: Check formal review status and core evidence separately; repeat at later scheduled reviews.

nodes.label: Revise and recheck
nodes.detail: Gather evidence, narrow claims or revise the agenda; handle an unsuccessful review through the formal process.

nodes.label: Original Contributions, Output Recognition and Scholarly Exchange
nodes.detail: Connect studies and verify original contributions and individual responsibility.

nodes.label: Dissertation Synthesis and Academic Integrity Checks
nodes.detail: Organize the thesis around evidence and complete applicable submission checks.

nodes.label: Preliminary Defence, Dissertation Review and Responses
nodes.detail: Follow local requirements for pre-defense, thesis review and responses.

nodes.label: Review resolved and defense eligibility confirmed?
nodes.detail: Follow the official outcome for revision, re-review or appeals.

nodes.label: Revise and recheck
nodes.detail: Respond point by point, add evidence and revise; arrange re-review or deferral as required.

nodes.label: Formal Defence, Revision Approval and Degree Application
nodes.detail: Defend after eligibility is confirmed, then complete corrections and degree procedures.

nodes.label: Post-defense corrections and submissions confirmed?
nodes.detail: Record degree-conferral status separately, based on the institution’s official decision.

nodes.label: Revise and recheck
nodes.detail: Revise and verify according to the defense decision; follow the required process for any further defense.

nodes.label: Research Archive, Handover and Future Development
nodes.detail: Verify recoverable records, handover responsibilities and future research directions.

flows.title: Literature: from search to research positioning
flows.summary: Connect search records, source checks, comparison matrices and topic decisions.
flows.note: Record published results, local replication results and untested hypotheses separately. If the problem is already solved, revise the question rather than merely renaming it.

nodes.label: Define the question and search boundaries
nodes.detail: Specify key concepts, synonyms, databases, date range and inclusion/exclusion criteria.

nodes.label: Search, deduplicate and screen
nodes.detail: Save search queries and dates, record inclusion/exclusion reasons and obtain lawful full-text access.

nodes.label: Read closely and check original sources
nodes.detail: Check methods, data, evaluation definitions, limitations and contrary evidence; trace citations.

nodes.label: Is key evidence covered and verifiable?
nodes.detail: Check representative studies and contrary findings. Reference counts do not establish quality.

nodes.label: Revise and review
nodes.detail: Extend the search, trace original sources or mark evidence as unverifiable. Do not cite fabricated references.

nodes.label: Build an evidence matrix and review
nodes.detail: Compare questions and methods, marking papers read, unavailable full texts and unresolved checks.

nodes.label: Position the research and define validation tasks
nodes.detail: Identify the closest work, differences, value and testable hypotheses.

nodes.label: Does the question still merit research?
nodes.detail: The difference is real, and the scope and resources support a meaningful test.

nodes.label: Revise and review
nodes.detail: Narrow the question, change direction or stop this candidate topic, preserving the reasoning.

nodes.label: Keep the reference collection current
nodes.detail: Save reference metadata, reading notes and reasons for changes in research positioning.

flows.title: Replication: from environment to evidence
flows.summary: Distinguish environment checks, offline recalculation, actual execution and research conclusions.
flows.note: Replication does not guarantee identical numerical results. Explain differences in data, configuration or evaluation, and limit claims accordingly. Retain failure and timeout records.

nodes.label: Define the replication target and baseline
nodes.detail: Identify the paper version, target claim, data license and evaluation definitions.

nodes.label: Freeze the environment and run a small test
nodes.detail: Record code version, dependencies, hardware, data splits, configuration and startup commands.

nodes.label: Do the small test and resource conditions pass?
nodes.detail: A successful installation is not a completed experiment.

nodes.label: Revise and review
nodes.detail: Identify dependency, data, access or computing-resource issues. Reduce the trial if needed and rerun it.

nodes.label: Run the predefined experiments
nodes.detail: Save actual commands, times, exit status, full logs and raw outputs.

nodes.label: Analyze results and differences
nodes.detail: Use the predefined rules for failures, statistical uncertainty and comparison conditions.

nodes.label: Check key claims against records
nodes.detail: Repeat key steps in the declared environment, or state the exact scope of offline recalculation.

nodes.label: Does the evidence support the current claims?
nodes.detail: Each result is traceable to a specific version and original record.

nodes.label: Revise and review
nodes.detail: Investigate differences, add experiments or narrow claims. Do not discard unfavorable cases to obtain a desired result.

nodes.label: Prepare a verifiable experiment package
nodes.detail: Include configuration, logs, analysis scripts, README, limitations and licenses.

edges.label: Return to environment and small test

flows.title: Engineering: from requirements to acceptance
flows.summary: Connect design, implementation, testing and acceptance for capstones and competition projects.
flows.note: Choose tools according to risk and task size. A working interface is partial evidence; delivery should cover core requirements, failure cases and usage boundaries.

nodes.label: Specify requirements and acceptance conditions
nodes.detail: Confirm user scenarios, scope, individual responsibility and measurable goals.

nodes.label: Detailed design and critical prototypes
nodes.detail: Describe interfaces, data, error handling and dependencies. Test high-risk elements first.

nodes.label: Can the design meet core acceptance conditions?
nodes.detail: Critical dependencies and the technical approach have passed small tests.

nodes.label: Revise and review
nodes.detail: Clarify requirements or change the design. Record the impact of significant scope changes and obtain agreement.

nodes.label: Implement a complete minimal user journey
nodes.detail: Expand through version control and task records while keeping run instructions usable.

nodes.label: Test and organize evidence
nodes.detail: Cover core functions, boundary cases and failures; record the environment and results.

nodes.label: Demonstrate and accept against requirements
nodes.detail: Check the deliverable version, explaining implemented scope, defects and limitations.

nodes.label: Do the core goals pass acceptance?
nodes.detail: Planned features are not described as already implemented.

nodes.label: Revise and review
nodes.detail: Fix defects and retest. If goals cannot be met, revise the scope and explanation, then seek renewed agreement.

nodes.label: Release or hand over the agreed version
nodes.detail: Confirm publication permission, dependency licenses, rollback procedures and receipt.

flows.title: Thesis submission: checks, review and defense
flows.summary: Connect file versions, formal checks, reviewer feedback and degree procedures.
flows.note: Institutions differ in whether they require a pre-defense or non-academic-error checks, and in the order of these steps. Confirm the applicable policy and what each check covers. Thesis checks, review, defense and degree conferral are distinct states.

nodes.label: Check eligibility, application window and procedures
nodes.detail: Confirm required outputs, pre-defense arrangements, platforms, templates and deadlines.

nodes.label: Complete the thesis and supervisory review
nodes.detail: Connect claims, references, figures and attachments to actual evidence.

nodes.label: Complete each required check separately
nodes.detail: Handle similarity screening, non-academic-error checks and AI disclosure separately, with reports tied to the same version.

nodes.label: Are eligibility and all required checks satisfied?
nodes.detail: Apply institutional criteria. Do not invent universal thresholds.

nodes.label: Revise and review
nodes.detail: Investigate the cause, revise, repeat screening or request a review. Check whether substantive changes require new screening.

nodes.label: Submit anonymously and receive reviews
nodes.detail: Check text, metadata, attachments and links; retain the version checksum and submission receipt.

nodes.label: Is defense eligibility formally confirmed?
nodes.detail: Follow official decisions on review, further review or appeals.

nodes.label: Revise and review
nodes.detail: Address each comment and seek further review or defer as required. Do not declare a pass yourself.

nodes.label: Apply for and attend the formal defense
nodes.detail: Submit materials, present and answer questions under the official eligibility decision, committee arrangements and notice.

nodes.label: Does the formal decision permit finalization?
nodes.detail: A conditional pass still requires every specified condition to be met.

nodes.label: Revise and review
nodes.detail: Revise, seek another review or reapply as required. A successful repeat defense cannot be guaranteed.

nodes.label: Finalize revisions and degree procedures
nodes.detail: Complete revisions, signatures and receipt. Degree status follows the institution's official decision.

nodes.label: Submit degree materials and archive research separately
nodes.detail: Confirm institutional submission and research-material acceptance, protecting unpublished and sensitive materials.

edges.label: Return to thesis revision and checks
Return to revision and formal review

flows.title: Routine work: tasks, feedback and next steps
flows.summary: Turn each discussion into deliverable tasks, owners, evidence and review dates.
flows.note: Students and supervisors agree on a working rhythm that fits coursework and research. Use institutional rules and designated channels for formal attendance, leave, practice and assessment.

nodes.label: Agree on goals and completion conditions
nodes.detail: Specify tasks, owners, inputs, deliverables, review dates and support needed.

nodes.label: Execute and retain process records
nodes.detail: Update actual versions and results daily. Report blockers, their impact and attempted solutions promptly.

nodes.label: Are inputs, resources and arrangements still workable?
nodes.detail: Seek help early when blocked. Do not fabricate progress after a deadline.

nodes.label: Revise and review
nodes.detail: Explain causes and alternatives. Agree on a smaller scope, a revised date or a necessary formal change.

nodes.label: Submit a weekly report and discussion points
nodes.detail: Distinguish facts, interpretations and plans; attach accessible evidence.

nodes.label: Discuss and record action items
nodes.detail: Record decisions, unresolved questions, revision locations, owners and deadlines.

nodes.label: Does the delivery meet the agreed conditions?
nodes.detail: Actual materials support completion status. Record official assessment outcomes separately.

nodes.label: Revise and review
nodes.detail: Address feedback item by item. Keep disputed conclusions pending confirmation and arrange another review.

nodes.label: Complete the review and plan the next cycle
nodes.detail: Record the evidence for completion; give continuing work a new set of goals.

flows.title: Archiving and handover: materials to acceptance
flows.summary: Ensure the recipient can locate, open and verify materials, with clear retention and access responsibilities.
flows.note: Submit degree materials and hand over research records separately. Keep public copies apart from controlled originals. Transfer access through organization-approved procedures; do not share personal account passwords.

nodes.label: Organize materials and version index
nodes.detail: List the thesis, code, data, logs, analyses, instructions, licenses and unfinished work.

nodes.label: Check permissions and visibility
nodes.detail: Separate public, team-controlled and restricted access. Remove sensitive information from public copies.

nodes.label: Are publication and transfer permissions clear?
nodes.detail: Having downloaded or accessed material does not grant permission to publish it.

nodes.label: Revise and review
nodes.detail: Obtain permission, de-identify or restrict access. Keep nonpublic material only in approved locations.

nodes.label: Prepare the archive and restoration instructions
nodes.detail: Add data provenance, versions, dependencies, commands, checksums, owners and retention periods.

nodes.label: Have the recipient test restoration and reproduction
nodes.detail: Open a sample of files, restore key materials using the instructions and verify core evidence.

nodes.label: Are materials complete and verifiable as documented?
nodes.detail: Directory screenshots, empty files and a successful upload do not replace acceptance checks.

nodes.label: Revise and review
nodes.detail: Add missing records and repeat acceptance. State the causes and impact of anything that cannot be restored.

nodes.label: Confirm receipt, access and outstanding responsibilities
nodes.detail: Record the accepted scope, pending tasks, account/equipment arrangements and limits of future contact.

nodes.label: Review backups and retention periodically
nodes.detail: Retain materials and control access according to licenses and institutional requirements; recheck restoration as agreed.

edges.label: Return to missing records and restoration instructions

flows.title: Joint training across institutions
flows.summary: Seven working steps connect hosting or sending arrangements, shared supervision, formal recognition and handover. Three checks show when to revise or seek confirmation.
flows.note: This is working guidance, not an approved institutional programme. Supervisory agreement, institutional approval, completed research and formal recognition are distinct. Apply the rules and authorised decisions relevant to each student; shared supervision does not itself confer a joint or double degree.

nodes.label: Identify the arrangement and roles
nodes.detail: Record hosting or sending roles, enrolment, awarding institution and scope.

nodes.label: Check requirements and procedures
nodes.detail: Confirm hosting, supervision eligibility, recognition and responsible offices.

nodes.label: Ready to start?
nodes.detail: Required approvals, resource access and hosting arrangements are documented.

nodes.label: Resolve missing conditions
nodes.detail: Obtain confirmation from the responsible office before starting dependent work.

nodes.label: Agree on the individual plan
nodes.detail: Set learning goals, tasks, responsibilities, deadlines and review evidence.

nodes.label: Work and obtain shared feedback
nodes.detail: Use shared task records and versions; track issues and actions on feedback.

nodes.label: Review progress and prepare materials
nodes.detail: Self-check, obtain supervisory feedback and prepare required submissions.

nodes.label: Do outputs meet the agreed checks?
nodes.detail: Evidence supports the conclusion; remaining comments and formal requirements are identified.

nodes.label: Revise work or the plan
nodes.detail: Record gaps, owners and review dates; complete required procedures for formal changes.

nodes.label: Complete applicable formal recognition
nodes.detail: Submit to the authorised offices and keep receipts, decisions and next steps.

nodes.label: Is recognition status resolved?
nodes.detail: Keep formal decisions or a documented basis for non-applicability; do not record an unsuccessful result as a pass.

nodes.label: Supplement, request review or replan
nodes.detail: Respond to missing items or use formal review channels; agree on interim and subsequent work.

nodes.label: Continue or complete the handover
nodes.detail: Follow the decisions into the next stage, archive records and confirm retention and access.

edges.label: Return to the plan and tasks

flows.title: From first contact to research collaboration
flows.summary: Six practical steps connect your interests with an agreed research or competition project. Two shared decisions keep the work suitable for both sides.
flows.note: This is an invitation to discuss collaboration, not a promise of a place, funding or admission. Timing and arrangements are agreed individually; pausing or concluding is a valid outcome. Formal procedures apply only where relevant.

nodes.label: Choose a question to explore
nodes.detail: Use the published research directions to describe your interests and learning goals.

nodes.label: Send a short introduction
nodes.detail: Describe your background, shareable work, availability, participation mode and language.

nodes.label: Discuss interests and expectations
nodes.detail: Discuss goals, preparation, supervision, resources and available time.

nodes.label: Can we agree on a suitable first task?
nodes.detail: Both sides understand the task and feedback arrangements, and its conditions can be met.

nodes.label: Adjust the direction, timing or preparation
nodes.detail: Narrow the task or build foundations; either side may close the discussion and reconnect later.

nodes.label: Complete the agreed small task
nodes.detail: Produce an explainable result, an honest work record and questions against the learning goal.

nodes.label: Review the work together
nodes.detail: Discuss the result, difficulties, individual contribution and support needed.

nodes.label: Do both sides want and have the capacity to continue?
nodes.detail: Confirm research fit, supervision capacity, task conditions and individual commitments.

nodes.label: Revise the plan or conclude the collaboration
nodes.detail: Record feedback and contributions; discuss a revised plan or finish with a useful summary.

nodes.label: Confirm collaboration and continue learning
nodes.detail: Agree on tasks and supervision; use the joint training guide when visiting, credit or degree procedures apply.
